bugs.title: Bot proposed slot before calling check_availability — slot collision on confirmation
bugs.description: At turns 6-7 the bot proposed 'sábado 13 de junio a las 10:20 con Marta' without any check_availability tool call (tool_evidence=[]). When the user confirmed after policy acceptance (turn 9), the book tool found the slot unavailable and rejected it. This is a classic optimistic-proposal / slot-race bug: the bot is fabricating slots from internal context/availability cache without real-time validation at proposal time.
bugs.root_cause_hypothesis: AvailabilityContextMiddleware may pre-hydrate a slot list into state that the LLM reads and presents without calling check_availability. The book tool correctly validates at commit time but the UX already told the user the slot was hers.

bugs.title: Dual-customer booking lands as single appointment with 2 service_ids — not 2 separate appointments
bugs.description: The scenario expected 2 separate appointments (one for Mónica, one for her husband) so they could be independently managed. The bot booked both services into a single appointment row (1 row, service_ids=[Corte Mujer UUID, Corte Hombre UUID]). This means if the husband needs to cancel independently, or wants a different stylist, there is no separate record to operate on. Expected outcome was multi_completed (2 appointments), actual is 1.
bugs.root_cause_hypothesis: The book tool does not support booking on behalf of a second unnamed customer in the same conversation. It appended the second service to the same appointment rather than creating two separate bookings for two distinct customers.

bugs.title: Excessive clarification loop (3 turns) before searching availability
bugs.description: Turns 1-3 are a 3-turn echo loop where the bot re-confirms the same information ('corte mujer / corte caballero') already provided in turn 1. This wastes 2 turns (14 turn budget consumed) and degrades UX for a straightforward dual-service scenario. Expected: 1 clarification turn maximum, then proceed to customer identification.
bugs.root_cause_hypothesis: Prompt rules may require explicit confirmation before proceeding for multi-intent messages, but the loop fires twice instead of once.

tool_calls_verdict: FAIL — check_availability not observed in tool_evidence; book was called but only once for a single combined appointment
